questiontext.text:
In triangle \(ABC\) the sides are \(a = BC = {@a@}\), \(b = CA = {@b@}\) and \(c = AB = {@c@}\).

The incircle (inradius \(r\), blue) is drawn. The excircle opposite \(A\) (exradius \(r_a\), red) is also drawn; the line \(ED\) is parallel to \(CB\) and tangent to this excircle on the far side, meeting the extensions of \(AB\) and \(AC\) at \(E\) and \(D\), with \(a' = ED = {@aprime@}\).

Find the ratio of the exradius \(r_a\) to the inradius \(r\). Give your answer as a fraction in lowest terms.

\( \dfrac{r_a}{r} = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Because \(ED \parallel CB\), triangles \(AED\) and \(ABC\) are similar, and the excircle opposite \(A\) is the incircle of the larger triangle \(AED\). Since \(r = \frac{\Delta}{s}\) scales linearly with the sides (as the semi-perimeter scales linearly and the area scales quadratically), the ratio of the two inradii is therefore the scale factor of the similarity, which is the ratio of any pair of corresponding sides:

\[ \frac{r_a}{r} \;=\; \frac{ED}{BC} \;=\; \frac{a'}{a} \;=\; \frac{{@aprime@}}{{@a@}} \;=\; {@ta1@}. \]

Equivalently, from \(r=\dfrac{\Delta}{s}\) and \(r_a=\dfrac{\Delta}{s-a}\) with \(s=\dfrac{a+b+c}{2}={@s@}\), the area \(\Delta\) cancels:

\[ \frac{r_a}{r} \;=\; \frac{\Delta/(s-a)}{\Delta/s} \;=\; \frac{s}{s-a} \;=\; \frac{a+b+c}{\,b+c-a\,} \;=\; {@ta1@}. \]

Notice that \(b\) and \(c\) are not needed for the first solution.

questionvariables.text: inr(t) := block([x:t[1],y:t[2],z:t[3],ss], ss:(x+y+z)/2, sqrt(ss*(ss-x)*(ss-y)*(ss-z))/ss); /* inradius of a triangle */ alltri : [[4,5,6],[5,6,7],[6,7,8],[4,6,7],[5,7,8],[6,8,9],[7,8,10],[5,6,8]]; /* drop any triangle with r = 1: then r_a = r_a/r, so the "found r_a" distractor would coincide with the correct answer. (All curated cases have r ~ 1.3..2.2.) */ data : sublist(alltri, lambda([t], is(float(inr(t)) # 1))); row : data[rand(length(data))+1]; a : row[1]; /* BC, opposite A (smallest side) */ b : row[2]; /* CA */ c : row[3]; /* AB */ s : (a+b+c)/2; /* semi-perimeter */ ratio : (a+b+c)/(b+c-a); /* = s/(s-a) = r_a/r (exact rational) */ recip : 1/ratio; /* r/r_a : the reciprocal misconception */ aprime : a*ratio; /* a' = ED = a * scale factor (may be fractional) */ area : sqrt(s*(s-a)*(s-b)*(s-c)); /* Heron area (an irrational surd) */ rin : area/s; /* inradius r : gave a radius, not the ratio */ rex : area/(s-a); /* exradius r_a : gave a radius, not the ratio */ ta1 : ratio;

node.description: Correct: r_a/r to 3 s.f. (1% relative tol)

truefeedback.text: That is \(\dfrac{r}{r_a}\), the reciprocal. The excircle is larger than the incircle, so \(\dfrac{r_a}{r} > 1\). Take the reciprocal of your value.

node.description: Diagnose: gave the exradius r_a itself (2% rel tol)

truefeedback.text: That looks like the exradius \(r_a\) itself, not the ratio. You still need to divide by the inradius: the answer is \(\dfrac{r_a}{r}\), a pure number with no length units.
